mainTopic: Whether daughters' support can be collected from movable property or only from land, and how the courts ruled in practice
overview: רב המנונא teaches that just as sons inherit only from land, daughters are supported only from land. Everyone objects, because sons obviously inherit everything. רב יוסף explains that he meant the כתובת בנין דכרין, which is collected only from land, and רב המנונא agrees. The גמרא then asks whether רב's support of orphan girls 'from the wheat of the עלייה' was a dowry measured by the father's status, as שמואל taught, or actual food based on the attic ruling that daughters are fed even from movables. A story about שמואל is brought as proof, but it is pushed off as being about a dowry. Then a series of practical cases follows: רב נחמן forces judges to reverse collections from movables, רבי יעקב בר אידי stops רבי אמי and רבי אסי, and רבי שמעון בן אליקים warns רבי אלעזר that a ruling made out of compassion could become permanent הלכה. Finally, אביי challenges רב יוסף's order to pay a daughter from dates on the mats. רב יוסף explains that he meant ripe dates still on the tree, which count as land.

steps.title: רב המנונא: daughters are supported only from land
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא teaches that sons inherit only from land, and in the same way daughters are supported only from land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף was sitting before רב המנונא. רב המנונא sat and said: Just as sons inherit only from land, so too daughters are supported only from land.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא makes a comparison: daughters' support comes only from land, just like sons' inheritance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main point is about daughters: their support can be collected from the father's land but not from his movable things. He backs this up with a comparison to sons, and that comparison is what the listeners will attack next.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הַמְנוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Yosef sat before Rav Hamnuna
and Rav Hamnuna sat and said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין הַבָּנִים יוֹרְשִׁין אֶלָּא מִן הַקַּרְקַע —
phrases.english: Just as sons inherit only from land,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אֵין הַבָּנוֹת נִיזּוֹנוֹת אֶלָּא מִן הַקַּרְקַע.
phrases.english: so too, daughters are supported only from land.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Daughters' support is collected only from land, just like sons' inheritance.

steps.title: Everyone objects: sons inherit everything, not just land
steps.stepSummary: The listeners protest: does a man's son inherit only if he left land? Of course sons inherit everything!
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone murmured against him: Is it only one who leaves land whose sons inherit him, and one who does not leave land, his sons do not inherit him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The audience attacks the comparison רב המנונא used, because sons obviously inherit movable things too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge goes after the first half of the statement, 'sons inherit only from land.' That is plainly false, since sons inherit all of their father's property. If the comparison falls apart, the ruling about daughters loses its support.
steps.confusionAlert: The listeners are not arguing about daughters. They are only objecting to the claim about sons.

phrases.english: Everyone murmured against him:

phrases.aramaic: דְּשָׁבֵיק אַרְעָא — הוּא דְּיָרְתִי לֵיהּ בְּנֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Is it only one who leaves land whose sons inherit him,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא שָׁבֵיק אַרְעָא — לָא יָרְתִי לֵיהּ בְּנֵיהּ?!
phrases.english: and one who does not leave land, his sons do not inherit him?!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that sons inherit only from land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sons plainly inherit movable property too, so the comparison is false.

steps.title: רב יוסף: maybe he meant the sons' כתובה inheritance
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף suggests that רב המנונא was talking about the כתובת בנין דכרין, not regular inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: Perhaps the Master was speaking about the כתובת בנין דכרין?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a different way to read רב המנונא's words so the objection goes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כתובת בנין דכרין is a special right: a woman's sons inherit her כתובה money in addition to their regular share. Like a כתובה, that right is collected only from land. If this is what 'sons inherit' meant, the comparison holds.

keyTerms.meaning: the 'male sons' כתובה': a woman's sons inherit her כתובה amount

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְדִלְמָא כְּתוּבַּת בְּנִין דִּכְרִין קָאָמַר מָר?!
phrases.english: Perhaps the Master was speaking about the כתובה of male sons?!
phrases.notes: These are a wife's sons, who inherit their mother's כתובה money on top of their regular share.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא כְּתוּבַּת בְּנִין דִּכְרִין קָאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 2 by reinterpreting step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Sons inherit' means regular inheritance, which includes movables.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Sons inherit' means the כתובת בנין דכרין, which is collected only from land.

steps.title: רב המנונא confirms רב יוסף's reading
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא agrees that this is exactly what he meant, praising רב יוסף as a great man.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The Master, who is a great man, knows what I am saying.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא says that רב יוסף understood him correctly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the first discussion. The comparison is between the sons' כתובה inheritance and daughters' support, both of which come only from land. The others had simply misunderstood him.
steps.whatToRemember: Daughters' support and the כתובת בנין דכרין are both collected only from land, according to רב המנונא.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The Master, who is a great man,
knows what I am saying.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר, דְּגַבְרָא רַבָּא הוּא, יָדַע מַאי קָאָמֵינָא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב המנונא meant the כתובת בנין דכרין, so his ruling that daughters are supported only from land stands.

steps.title: רב supported girls from 'the wheat of the עלייה'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף reports that רב gave support from 'wheat of the עלייה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף said: רב gave support from the wheat of the עלייה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new report about how רב acted in practice. It sets up the question in the next step about what 'עלייה' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wheat is a movable thing, not land. So רב seems to have supported daughters from movables, which raises a question compared to רב המנונא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: upper room, attic; also hints at 'raising up' or status

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef said:
Rav gave support from the wheat of the עלייה.
phrases.notes: He means orphan daughters, supported from wheat even though wheat is not land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף: רַב זָן מֵחִיטֵּי דַעֲלִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related practice of רב about supporting daughters
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב supported orphan girls from wheat, which is movable property.

steps.title: First possibility: it was a dowry, measured by the father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב's support was פרנסה (a dowry), with 'עלייה' meaning the father's status, as שמואל taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Was it a dowry? And what does 'עלייה' mean? From the father's status, like שמואל. For שמואל said: For a dowry, we estimate based on the father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a question and offers the first side: maybe רב was giving a dowry, not food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this side, 'עלייה' comes from 'עילויא', the father's standing. שמואל taught that a daughter's dowry is measured by what the father would have given, based on his status. If so, this does not tell us anything about food support from movables.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked to them (the scholars)
dowry, money given so a daughter can marry

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
Was it a dowry,
and what does 'עלייה' mean? From the status of the father,
in line with שמואל.
As שמואל said: For a dowry, we estimate based on the father.
phrases.notes: We look at how generous and wealthy the father was to decide how big the dowry should be.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what kind of support step 5 describes
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was רב's support a dowry or actual food, and what does 'עלייה' mean?

steps.title: Second possibility: real food, based on the attic ruling
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe it was actual food, and 'עלייה' refers to the attic where the Sages ruled that daughters may be supported from movables.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it was actual food, and what does 'עלייה' mean? From the good things said in the attic. For רב יצחק בר יוסף said: In the attic they enacted that daughters should be supported from movable property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of its question: maybe רב was giving real food support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'עלייה' means the actual attic where the Sages met and made a תקנה: daughters may be fed from movables, not only land. If so, this goes against רב המנונא's rule that daughters are supported only from land. The next step tries to settle the question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This second side directly disagrees with רב המנונא, so the answer decides whether daughters can collect food from movables.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it was actual food,
and what does 'עלייה' mean?
It is from the good things that were said in the attic.
As Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֲלִיָּיה הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ בָּנוֹת נִיזּוֹנוֹת מִן הַמִּטַּלְטְלִין.
phrases.english: In the attic they enacted that daughters should be supported from movable property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the question begun in step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'עלייה' refers to the attic ruling that allows food support from movables

steps.title: A story with שמואל seems to prove daughters are fed from movables
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a story where שמואל told רבי בנאי to 'feed' the orphan daughters from movable goods. It suggests this means real food, so שמואל agrees with רב יצחק בר יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי בנאי, the brother of רבי חייא בר אבא, was holding movable goods that belonged to orphans. They came before שמואל, and he told him: 'Go, feed them.' Doesn't this mean food, and שמואל holds like רב יצחק בר יוסף?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to settle the question from steps 6 and 7 with a real story about שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל told רבי בנאי to support the daughters from movable goods. If 'feed' means real food, then שמואל agrees with the ruling made in the attic (step 7) that daughters are fed even from movables.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא brings a source to answer a question
Movable property, things you can pick up and carry (not land)
Is it not? The גמרא is suggesting a reading

phrases.english: Come and hear:
In the hands of Rabbi Banai
the brother of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba
there were movable goods belonging to orphans.
They came before Shmuel.
He said to him: Go, feed [them].
phrases.notes: שמואל is talking to רבי בנאי, telling him to support the orphan daughters from the goods he was holding.

phrases.english: Is it not that this means for food,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִדְרַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף סְבִירָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: and he holds like Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef?
phrases.notes: This points back to the ruling made in the attic (step 7), that daughters may be fed even from movables.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the either/or question from steps 6 and 7 with a story about שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: That daughters are given food (מזונות) from movable property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's instruction to רבי בנאי, 'זיל זון', about orphans' movable goods.

steps.title: No, שמואל meant a dowry, not food
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: שמואל was talking about a dowry, and he follows his own rule that a dowry is measured by the father's status.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. There, it was about a dowry. And שמואל follows his own reasoning, because שמואל said: for a dowry, we estimate based on the father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading 'feed' as giving a dowry, not food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'זון' can mean support in general, it may mean a dowry (פרנסה). שמואל's own known rule about dowries fits this reading, so the story proves nothing about food from movables.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, his known opinion elsewhere
We estimate based on the father, judging by what he would have given

steps.confusionAlert: 'Feed them' does not have to mean food here. The גמרא reads it as 'give them their dowry'.

phrases.english: No, there it was for a dowry.
And Shmuel follows his own reasoning,
for Shmuel said:
For a dowry, we estimate based on the father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 8 by reading the story differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof from שמואל's story.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'זון' means food; it can mean a dowry, which fits שמואל's known rule.

steps.title: רב נחמן forces judges to undo collecting from movables
steps.stepSummary: Courts in נהרדעא and פומבדיתא collected support for daughters from movables. רב נחמן ordered them to reverse it, or he would take their houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case in נהרדעא, and the judges of נהרדעא ruled to collect. In פומבדיתא, רב חנא בר ביזנא collected. רב נחמן said to them: Go, give it back. If not, I will take your mansions from you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of real cases where judges collected for the daughters from movables, and רב נחמן strongly overturned them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These judges acted as if daughters may be supported from movables. רב נחמן's sharp threat shows he held that this is not the הלכה, so the money taken was taken wrongly and must be returned.

keyTerms.meaning: A real case, an actual incident

phrases.english: There was a case in Nehardea,
and the judges of Nehardea ruled.
phrases.notes: They ruled that the daughters get support from the movables their father left.

phrases.english: In Pumbedita,
and Rav Chana bar Bizna collected.
Rav Nachman said to them:
Go, reverse it,
and if not
I will collect your mansions from you.
phrases.notes: He means he would take the judges' own houses to pay back the people they wrongly ruled against.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof was rejected, the גמרא moves to practical cases showing how the הלכה was actually decided.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן held that daughters are not supported from movable property, and judges who collected from movables must reverse it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows in practice that the attic ruling about movables was not accepted as practical הלכה by רב נחמן.

steps.title: Don't rule where רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש held back
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי wanted to rule that daughters are fed from movables. רבי יעקב בר אידי stopped them, since רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש never acted on this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי thought to give food from movables. רבי יעקב בר אידי said to them: A matter that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש did not put into practice, you are going to put into practice?!
steps.whatsHappening: Two more sages wanted to rule that daughters are fed from movables, and they are stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב בר אידי's argument is about practice: if the great sages before them never ruled this way in a real case, it is not safe to do so now. This backs up רב נחמן, so in practice daughters are not fed from movables.

keyTerms.meaning: To feed, to give food support
Acting in practice, issuing a real ruling

steps.whatToRemember: Both stories end the same way: in practice, courts did not collect food for daughters from the father's movable property.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi
thought to give food from movables.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi said to them:
A matter that Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish
did not act upon in practice,
you are going to act upon it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי סְבוּר לְמֵיזַן מִמִּטַּלְטְלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second practical story that agrees with רב נחמן's ruling in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, we do not rule that daughters are fed from movable property, since the great sages never acted on it.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר is warned not to rule from compassion
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר wanted to let daughters be fed from מטלטלין. רבי שמעון בן אליקים told him he knew this came from compassion and not strict law, but students might see it and make it permanent הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר thought he would rule that daughters are fed from movable goods. רבי שמעון בן אליקים said to him: 'My teacher, I know you are not doing this by strict law, only out of compassion. But the students might see it and set it as הלכה for all generations.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story, like step 11, where a great sage wanted to feed daughters from מטלטלין and was stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story adds a reason why such a ruling is a problem. רבי אלעזר's ruling would have been a kind act and not the real law, but students watching would think it is the law. So the strict rule stays: daughters are not fed from movables.

keyTerms.meaning: The strict letter of the law
Acting out of compassion or mercy
They will set it as the law for future generations

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a judge must think about how others will learn from his ruling, and not only about the case in front of him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar thought to feed [the daughters] from movable property.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְיָקִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim said before him:
My teacher, I know about you
that you are not acting by the strict law,
but out of compassion.
However, perhaps the students will see
and establish it as the law for generations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third practical story, after steps 10 and 11, confirming that the practice of feeding daughters from movables was stopped
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ruling to feed daughters from מטלטלין would only be compassion, not law, and must be avoided so students do not make it permanent הלכה.

steps.title: רב יוסף orders support from the dates on the mats
steps.stepSummary: A daughter's case came before רב יוסף, and he told the brothers to give her support from the dates on the drying mats.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain case came before רב יוסף. He told them: 'Give her from the dates that are on the mats.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of רב יוסף that seems to let a daughter be fed from movables. This sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dates spread out on mats to dry have already been picked, so they look like plain מטלטלין. That seems to go against the conclusion just reached, that daughters are not fed from movables.

keyTerms.meaning: Mats, where picked dates are spread out to dry

phrases.english: A certain [case] came before Rav Yosef,
He said to them: Give her
phrases.notes: "Them" means the dead man's sons, the heirs.

phrases.english: from the dates that are on the mats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ruling that seems to go against the conclusion that daughters are not fed from movables
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף told the heirs to support the daughter from the dates on the mats.

steps.title: אביי: Even a creditor could not collect this way
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף: if a בעל חוב came to collect in this situation, would you let him take movables from orphans? Surely not, so a daughter should not either.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: 'If this were a creditor in the same situation, would you, Master, give it to him?'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's ruling by comparing the daughter to a creditor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בעל חוב has a strong claim, yet he cannot collect from the orphans' מטלטלין. A daughter has a weaker claim, so she certainly should not collect from them. The dates on the mats are movables, so how could רב יוסף give them to her?

keyTerms.meaning: A creditor, someone who is owed money
In a case like this one
Master, a respectful way to address one's teacher

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִילּוּ בַּעַל חוֹב הֲוָה כִּי הַאי גַּוְונָא,
phrases.english: If it were a creditor in a case like this,
would the Master have given it to him?
phrases.notes: The answer he expects is "no." Orphans' movables are not taken even for a creditor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילּוּ בַּעַל חוֹב הֲוָה כִּי הַאי גַּוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's ruling from step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's order to pay the daughter from dates on the mats
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A creditor, whose claim is stronger, cannot collect from orphans' movables, so a daughter certainly cannot.

steps.title: רב יוסף: I meant dates ready for the mats
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that he meant dates still on the tree that are ripe and ready to be picked and put on the mats, not dates already lying there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'I was talking about dates that are fit for the mats.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי by explaining what he really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ripe dates still attached to the tree are not yet movables. They count as part of the land. So paying the daughter from them is paying from קרקע, which is allowed, and the ruling does not go against the law.
steps.whatToRemember: The law stays the same: daughters are fed from land, not from מטלטלין. Even רב יוסף's dates ruling only covers fruit still attached to the ground.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב יוסף let the daughter take picked fruit. He meant ripe fruit still on the tree, which counts as land.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I was speaking of [dates] that are fit for the mats.
phrases.notes: He means dates still on the tree, ripe enough to be picked and laid out to dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by redefining the case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the dates were still attached to the ground
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף gave the daughter picked dates, which are movables
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant ripe dates still attached to the tree, which count as land, so the ruling fits the law
